summary: Black Rock Studio and Disney Interactive's destructible-environment arcade racer, released as Split/Second in North America and Split/Second: Velocity in Europe, with PC/HD console, PSP, iOS, Java, and cloud routes.

entries.title: Split/Second: Velocity
entries.definitive_edition: Windows PC release with available DLC plus PSP exclusive-track check

emulation.emulator: Native Windows / RPCS3 / Xenia / PPSSPP / Java ME emulator
emulation.notes: Run Windows natively for the main route; use PPSSPP for the PSP-exclusive track and mode checks.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Windows PC route with DLC, PPSSPP for secondary content

primary.version: PC release with DLC/Ultimate Edition content where available
primary.why: Split/Second released for Windows, PlayStation 3, Xbox 360, iOS, PSP, OnLive, and Java ME. Windows is the highest-fidelity route, with DLC/Ultimate Edition content for the main version; PSP is a secondary route because it adds an extra Docks-based track and PSP-specific mode/rules changes.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows version at the highest stable settings with available DLC installed; use LAN/VPN-style workarounds for multiplayer if needed, and sample PSP separately for its exclusive track/mode differences.

secondary.exclusive_content: PSP port with an extra track based on the Docks environment plus PSP-specific gameplay modes/rule/physics changes.
secondary.what_to_play: Play the PSP-exclusive Docks track and sample the portable-specific modes.
secondary.why: The Windows route has better fidelity and DLC access, but PSP has sourced exclusive content and design changes.

all_releases.fidelity: PC release with configurable fidelity and access to main-version DLC/Ultimate Edition content where available.

all_releases.reason: skip: console route and no sourced content advantage over Windows/PSP secondary plan.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Windows is the best main-fidelity route and can include DLC, while PSP has an extra Docks-based track and portable-specific modes/changes.

entries.remaster_caveats: The Steam version lacks online matchmaking support; use LAN/VPN-style options for online preservation if needed. The planned sequel was cancelled.
